correctness.rationale: Uniform ranked endpoint pairings admit an explicit bijection with all 3^(n-1) ternary words exactly when no three intervals overlap. The resulting carrier process is a caterpillar forest with independent symbols. Binomial and geometric formulas follow by direct letter counting; the degree spectrum comes from a geometric run terminated by an independent equally likely B/N choice. Finite-dependent truncation proves fixed-degree laws and disjoint-block/union-bound estimates prove both logarithmic extremes. The standalone code independently enumerated 1..7 intervals and 1..10 ternary code lengths and passed 664317 exact assertions. Computation supports finite cases; infinite statements rest on the written proof.

evidence: Diaconis–Holmes–Janson (2011) state typical edge density 1/3 and n/2-sized clique asymptotics, which concern unconditioned dense graphs.

Korbel–Mörters (2020) prove a general product-of-downstep-heights path formula. It covers path events and thus makes the base height-two count non-novel in isolation, but stops short of graph degree laws.
Iliopoulos thesis discusses unconditioned degree and clique statistics, not the triangle-free conditional degree spectrum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest primary overlap is the more general formula for the one-dimensional open-pair-count path. The present degree spectrum and extremes depend on which specific interval survives each paired closing, data discarded by the path alone. Neither unconditional graph-limit results nor the different random-interval services model imply the reported rare-conditioned graph statements as their own special cases.

originality.rationale: The complete conditional graph/degree/extreme-scale law was not located in the inspected literature or previously published mathematical records. The 2020 sock-path formula subsumes the weighted Dyck-path part and indirectly the height-two count, which are credited and not claimed alone as novel. Its stated theorems do not provide the carrier graph degree mixture, limiting empirical degree probabilities, or simultaneous distinct logarithmic maximum-degree/component-size scales. Prior graph-limit and random-interval results are unconditioned. Historical priority remains qualified owing to inaccessible 1988 and 1990 full texts and possible implicit corollaries.
residual_risks: The restricted-path count and binomial component law are covered or immediately implied by the earlier sock-sorting path formula and are not presented as standalone originality.
The 1988 and 1990 original random-interval articles were not fully accessible. Their uninspected parts could contain an equivalent conditional graph result.

The particular combination of a conditioned degree distribution and two logarithmic extrema might be implicit in broader matching/sock path literature; no decisive stronger statement was located in the inspected primary texts.

value.rationale: Conditioning the standard dense iid interval-intersection graph on the natural bipartite/triangle-free constraint is structurally motivated. The uniform ternary renewal model provides an exact conditional graph sampler, complete component- and vertex-degree spectra, and two genuinely different extremal scales, clarifying the topology under a very rare event. This goes beyond a finite count, arbitrary slice or routine normalization check and can benchmark rare-condition algorithms.
